note: Source: Anthropic research post 'Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins' (2026-10-16), https://www.anthropic.com/research/ecdsa-curve-origins. Text saved at llm-wiki/raw/assets/ecdsa-curve-origins/article-text.txt. Headline numbers: 1,842 (P-256 draw), 160 bits per seed, 10 prime-curve seeds, 876 (skipped usable draw). Claims are Anthropic's own reported results; the P-256 draw and timestamp were re-checked by running the post's own reproduction code (seed C49D3608...7E90 reproduced).

claims.l01: Intro: seeds provided by the NSA with no explanation; people wondered if curves had deliberate backdoors (What this means).
claims.l02: Claude found the seeds: output of lrand48 seeded with a Unix timestamp.
claims.l03: Intro: ECDSA adopted by NIST in 2000 as part of FIPS 186-2, which lists standard elliptic curves.
claims.l04: Intro: a seed whose hash defines coefficient b; seeds provided by the NSA with no explanation. P-256 seed C49D3608 86E70493 6A6678E1 139D26B7 819F7E90.
claims.l05: Intro: the rumour (Solinas 2015) of a hash of a humorous passphrase such as 'Bob and Jerry rule'; How it was found: searches for the phrase came up empty.
claims.l06: How it was found: Claude guessed a PRNG that shipped with 1990s C libraries; the seeds came from lrand48.
claims.l07: How it was found: lrand48 is a linear congruential generator that returns the top 31 bits of a 48-bit state.
claims.l08: How it was found: prime-curve seeds kept fewer bits (lrand48() >> 23); recovering the state of a truncated LCG is solved with LLL lattice reduction.
claims.l09: How it was found: the LCG runs backwards; every srand48 initialization was a Unix timestamp between May 1997 and April 1998.
claims.l10: Claude found the seeds: P-256 required 1,842 iterations; reproduction code: P-256 1997-08-16 01:52:34, n=1842.
claims.l11: How it was found: 'Each recovered 48-bit state regenerates all 160 bits of its seed, which does not happen by chance.' Receipt.
claims.l12: What this means: 'These findings make that much less plausible.'
claims.l13: Open questions: B-163 seed unexplained; base points of P-224, P-256, P-384, P-521 and binary curves unknown (P-192 and five X9.62 base points recovered); candidate 876 also viable, criteria unknown.
